items.title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Micron Next?
items.summary: Micron Technology may be the next tech stock to announce a stock split, following SanDisk's recent 8-for-1 split announcement. Trading above $700 per share, Micron's strong fundamentals—including 379% year-over-year revenue growth, AI infrastructure demand, and multiyear strategic customer agreements—support potential further stock price appreciation toward $1,000+, which would justify a split. The company trades at a compelling 4.5 forward P/E ratio despite high growth rates.

items.title: DOW's Shares Surge 41% YTD: What's Driving the Momentum?
items.summary: Dow Inc. (DOW) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of 71 cents, beating estimates of 64 cents and reversing a year-ago loss. The company's performance is driven by higher prices, cost-reduction initiatives, and advantaged feedstock positions in the Americas. Dow expects $700 million in 2026 transformation benefits following $450 million in gains through Q3, with strategic investments in high-growth areas like AI infrastructure and specialty silicones.

items.title: Embraer Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates, Revenues Beat, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Embraer (EMBJ) missed Q3 earnings expectations with 40 cents per ADS versus consensus of 87 cents, though revenues grew 17.2% to $2.35 billion. The company delivered 66 aircraft and achieved a record $35.7 billion backlog. EMBJ raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $8.4-$8.6 billion and increased free cash flow outlook to at least $700 million, earning a Zacks Rank #1 Strong Buy rating.

items.title: Is CNH Industrials Stock Worth Buying After Q3 2026 Results?
items.summary: CNH Industrial is strengthening its agricultural equipment business through precision technology investments and a planned construction equipment joint venture with Kobelco, which should generate ~$700 million in cash for debt reduction. However, weak regional demand (particularly in South America), tariff pressures, rising credit risks, and working capital challenges continue to constrain financial performance, leading to a neutral investment outlook.

items.title: Smurfit Westrock: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Smurfit Westrock reported full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $4.7 billion, facing a $700 million energy and freight cost headwind. The company is offsetting these pressures through paper price increases of $170 per ton and leveraging structural advantages including European regulatory expertise, Latin American forestry assets, and integrated supply chains to rebuild profitability in 2027.

items.title: Kraft Heinz: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Kraft Heinz announced the divestiture of its North American coffee business to One Rock while retaining a 30% stake, allowing the company to focus capital on higher-growth core brands. The company is deploying $700 million in brand and marketing investments with data-driven adjustments to pricing strategies. Management expects input cost inflation slightly above 5% next year and plans to rely on productivity gains before implementing targeted price increases, though price hikes appear inevitable in 2027.

items.title: Can ZBRA's Strong Cash Generation Drive More Growth and Returns?
items.summary: Zebra Technologies (ZBRA) raised its 2026 free cash flow guidance to at least $1 billion from $900 million, driven by 25.3% year-over-year growth in H1 2026 free cash flow to $361 million. The company plans approximately $700 million in share repurchases for 2026, demonstrating strong capital allocation and shareholder returns.

items.title: The Nasdaq Composite Just Plunged Almost 700 Points in One Day: Is a Stock Market Crash Imminent?
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite dropped 694 points (2.6%) on October 22, 2026, marking its largest daily decline since June. While the stock market has rallied significantly since 2022 driven by AI infrastructure spending, historical indicators suggest elevated crash risk: the S&P 500's CAPE Ratio near 43 (vs. historical average of 17.44) and margin debt at record $1.502 trillion. However, the article emphasizes that downturns are normal and historically resolve quickly, with bull markets lasting 3.6 times longer than bear markets on average.

items.title: Up 3,700%, Should You Buy Sandisk Right Now?
items.summary: Sandisk stock has surged 3,700% since its February 2025 spinoff from Western Digital, driven by AI-driven demand for flash storage and strong financial performance. However, the article cautions investors that memory and storage stocks are historically volatile and prone to severe downturns when industry cycles turn, suggesting the current boom may not be sustainable.

items.title: IBM Q3 Beat Highlights Software Growth and a Stronger Cash Outlook
items.summary: IBM delivered better-than-expected Q3 2026 results with EPS up 11% to $2.95 and revenues growing 4.7% to $17.10 billion. Software revenues accelerated 9% driven by Red Hat (11% growth) and Data (20% growth), while free cash flow improved by $700 million to $3 billion. The company raised full-year guidance for Software growth (7%-8%) and free cash flow (>$1 billion growth). However, Consulting growth remained modest and IBM Z revenues declined 19% year-over-year.

items.title: Equifax: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Equifax reported Q3 2026 earnings with diversified markets revenue growing 8% year-over-year. The company secured $550 million in annual government contract value for workforce verification services, deployed AI tools to improve operational efficiency and raise profitability guidance, and saw rapid adoption of VantageScore among mortgage lenders. Management expects significant upside when mortgage rates decline, with potential for over $1 billion in incremental mortgage revenue and $700 million in margin expansion.

items.title: Why Cleveland-Cliffs Stock Popped Today
items.summary: Cleveland-Cliffs stock surged over 16% after reporting adjusted earnings of $0.28 per share, beating estimates of $0.21. The company's adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $612 million in Q3, with expectations to exceed $700 million in Q4. Strong steel prices and tariffs limiting imports are driving robust 2027 outlook with over $4 billion in projected adjusted EBITDA.
